newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Business leaders call for APEC barrier-busting.
newsitem.headline: Business leaders call for APEC barrier-busting.

text.p: Asia-Pacific business leaders applauded APEC's push to remove tariff barriers in the region on Friday but called for more action to remove obstacles to trade and investment.

Heads of multi-national companies from across the Pacific Rim, meeting under the auspices of the annual APEC conference in the Philippines, said they were keen to cooperate more closely in the development of the Asia-Pacific region.
But addressing several hundred delegates at the APEC Business Forum (ABF), the business leaders said there were still barriers to investment that needed to be removed.
Opening the ABF, Philippine President Fidel Ramos earlier urged businesses to help build the Asia-Pacific's trade and infrastructure in cooperation with its governments.
The ABF is meeting ahead of the summit of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Subic Bay, north of Manila, on Monday.
Maurice Greenberg, chairman and chief executive of American International Group Inc, said economic and social development could only advance with the help of private capital.
Private companies needed a helping hand to come up with necessary investment, he said. For example, government-backed agencies could help to insure foreign investors against political risk, he said.
"Governments could do more to create a real partnership with the
private sector to generate more private risk capital."

He quoted a recent World Bank study which estimated east Asia alone would need an infusion of some $1.5 trillion of infrastructure investment by the year 2004. He said the private sector would eventually need to fund around a fifth of this.

"One conclusion is unmistakeable -- there will be an acute shortfall of such private funds unless major steps are taken soon to facilitate an increase in such funding from capital suppliers," he said.
"Private capital will only flow to where an adequate return can be achieved," he said.

Greenberg, who heads one of the United States' largest financial services and insurance groups, said insurance companies and pension funds would play a major role in supplying the required capital providing the conditions were right.
These conditions included predictable tax regimes, effective judicial systems, enforceable business codes, ways of resolving business disputes and investment protection, he said.
He also called for the development of vibrant capital markets in the emerging economies of Asia to help generate such funds.
Minoru Murofushi, president of Japan's Itochu Corp trading house, told the forum that APEC was moving in the right direction but businesses still faced huge obstacles.
"In day-to-day business, we still encounter many, many impediments to cross-border trade," he said. He agreed that the gap between government funds and public needs was enormous.
"Huge infusions of private capital are needed to fill the gap," he said.
Jing Shuping, chairman of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, said existing barriers to trade should be removed and the emergence of new barriers should be prevented.
"The cooperation among the APEC members in removing barriers should be strengthened," he said.
